searchText: What is the planned inflation rate of ETH2 and what is the current inflation rate of ETH1 (only counting block rewards)? <@!301186049323958275> current supply of ETH according to CoinMarketCap is 114,405,763. About 4,959,985 has been created in the last 12 months based on the data I collected. 4,959,985/114,405,763 = 4.34%. Wouldn't that be the approximate current inflation rate only counting block rewards? Is that 5M minted ETH block reward only, not transaction fees? Correct. I took the info from the averages I calculated. Block/Uncle rewards averaged over the last 12 months is 13589 per day which is the total i used and multiplied by 365 to get the whole year. For additional reference, 1/21/2020 had those same rewards equal 13461 on that day. If you do 4 per minute x 60 minutes x 24 x 2 eth BR, you get 11520. So either the block times have averaged shorter than 15 seconds or the uncle rewards are a significant portion of the BRs. Average block time is under 15 seconds. I think it is closer to 13 seconds but I don't remember exactly. Eth2 ~~inflation~~ APR depends on number of validators. It's currently at around 8%. No it is fixed, the more validators the lower the rewards. I don't believe it is linear? Hmm, really 8%? I thought it was closer to 1%? It can't be 8%... that is the same order of magnitude as staker interest, which would mean that the majority of ETH is staking, which isn't the case at all. Current APR appears to be ~9.3% on 2.8M ETH. That comes out to something like 0.23% inflation. Yes, sorry, I was talking about APR. See eip-2982 issuance discussion https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2982#issuance ~1.5% inflation assuming 100% staking if I am reading that right? <@!333694584607604738> or <@!360491619402776577> , you can poke <@!601121887141232672> for the recording of today's call *poking* <@!601121887141232672> <dankrad> stateless ethererum? *poke* @rjdrost too
